title: And the Glory of the Lord
description: The first chorus of Handel's Messiah (1741), for 4 singers in Handel's own voice parts: its four tunes ("And the glory of the Lord", "shall be revealed", "and all flesh shall see it together" and "for the mouth of the Lord hath spoken it") pass from part to part and come together at the end. The orchestra is left out; it is in Handel's own key, A, as choirs sing it.

credits.words: the Bible (Isaiah 40:5, King James Version), as Charles Jennens chose them for Messiah
credits.arrangement: Handel's own four voice parts, from Ebenezer Prout's edition (Novello, 1902)

licence.words: public domain: the King James Version (1611), Isaiah 40:5, as Charles Jennens (died 1773) chose it for Messiah; sung as Prout's 1902 score prints it under the notes, with Handel's "glo-ry of", the "ry" and "of" sung on one note, which Prout restored (preface, p. vi), and "re-veal'd" where the soprano's bar 33 prints it; the same words in the 1750 Covent Garden wordbook (Messiah. An Oratorio, p. 4, read from archive.org/details/bim_eighteenth-century_messiah-an-oratorio-as_jennens-charles_1750); in the UK the KJV is under Crown letters patent (a question with our lawyer, as for The Lord Bless You)
licence.tune: public domain: Handel died 1759; "composed in the year 1741" (Prout's title page)
licence.arrangement: Handel's own four voice parts as Ebenezer Prout edited them (Novello, 1902; Handel died 1759, Prout died 1909; public domain), every pitch, rhythm and word kept, in Handel's own key, A major, as choirs sing it (Hillel, 2026-11-18): the beginner ranges are a guide here, not a reason to transpose, and the notes outside them are Handel's own writing (listed below). The orchestra is left out, as in the Ave verum: its opening ten bars (the alto enters alone, in bar 11), and its two interludes, bars 39 to 42 and 74 to 75, each sung as one bar's rest. The closing Adagio (bars 136 to 138, "hath spoken it") is written half as slow again, one and a half times its printed values, since a song has one tempo, and its last chord, under the fermata, is held 4 beats. Ties are joined into one note. The chords come from the four voices on each beat, with Handel's bass line (the orchestra's Bassi, read from the same pages) where the bass voice rests. Breaths written in for beginners where a line ran past 10 seconds (singable.py rule 2): the note before gives up a beat at 100, or half a beat with the next pickup coming half a beat later (rule 1): before "shall be revealed" in every part in bar 36, and the tenor's in bar 17 ("Lord" gives up a beat); the alto's "revealed, | be revealed" (bar 27) and "revealed, | and the glory" (bar 33); "of the Lord | hath spoken it" in the tenor and bass (bars 55 and 71) and the soprano (bar 61); the soprano's "together; | For the mouth" (bar 57), "together, | the mouth" (bar 83) and "together, | For the mouth" (bar 124); the tenor's "together, | the mouth" (bar 68), "of the Lord, | shall be revealed" (bar 97) and "together, | together" (bar 122); "of the Lord, | and all flesh" in the alto and tenor (bar 79); the alto's "the mouth | of the Lord" (bar 97), "hath spoken it, | and all flesh" (bar 102) and "of the Lord | shall be revealed" (bar 113); "revealed, | and all flesh" (tenor) and "revealed, | for the mouth" (bass) in bar 119, and the bass's "of the Lord | hath spoken it" (bar 122); "hath spoken it, | for the mouth" in the soprano and alto (bar 129). None falls inside a melisma. Accepted exceptions (singable.py): rule 4: Handel's own ranges, 71 notes outside the beginner ones: the soprano's F sharp 5 (bars 62, 83 to 86, 99, 101, 109 and 112, among them four bars held on "the mouth of the Lord", 83 to 86), G sharp 5 (bar 109) and top A5 on "Lord" (bar 110), 14 notes; the tenor's F sharp 4 (bars 18, 29, 34, 35, 56, 71, 73, 98, 117, 128, 130 to 133, 136 and 137, among them the held "spo-" of the Adagio) and G sharp 4 (bar 33), 18 notes; the bass's B3 (bars 20, 23, 24, 34, 37, 56, 68 to 71, 73, 79 to 82, 101, 132 and 134), C sharp 4 (bars 24, 35, 72 and 131 to 134), D4 (bars 62, 130 to 133 and the Adagio's held "spo-", 136), D sharp 4 (bar 35) and E4 ("Lord", bar 36), 39 notes; the alto none; and the times held near the top that go with them (the soprano's "mouth of the Lord", 5.1 s, the bass's and tenor's "spo-", 5.1 s), and the soprano, tenor and bass sitting above the middle of the beginner ranges, as Handel's chorus does; rule 5: 149: Handel's melismas in the alto (44 notes), tenor (49) and bass (29), on "revealed", "flesh", "Lord" and "spoken", and the leaps of his themes and cadences (27: among them the alto's octave into "glory" in bar 34 and its sixths into "ed," and "to-" in bars 27, 55 and 71, the tenor's sixth up to "spo-" in bar 56, the bass's octave drops inside "veal-" in bar 101 and on "ken" in bar 137); rule C: 7: Handel's parallel fifths between soprano and alto into bar 78 (F sharp over B to B over E at his pitch), his crossings (the tenor over the alto in bars 33 and 77, the alto's "of" over the soprano's "it," in bar 98), and the G sharp in alto and bass in bar 100, the third of E there, not a leading note
licence.source: The Messiah, a sacred oratorio, composed in the year 1741 by G. F. Handel, edited, and the additional accompaniments largely re-written, by Ebenezer Prout (full score; title page, leaf n6; London: Novello and Company, Limited, and New York: Novello, Ewer and Co.; "Copyright, 1902, by Novello and Company, Limited"; preface signed London, April 1902), No. 4, Chorus, "And the glory of the Lord", pp. 19 to 35, Allegro, crotchet = 100, in A major, 3/4, 138 bars; the four voice parts (soprano, alto and bass in the treble and bass clefs, the tenor in the tenor clef) read from the University of Toronto Faculty of Music copy at archive.org/details/messiahsacredora00hand_0 (pages 19 to 35, leaves n44 to n60), and the orchestra's bass line (Bassi) read there too for the chords where the bass voice rests; written here in A, as printed
